title: 360 Pano mirroring: patching and refining a mis-stitched 360 panorama
summary: The video demonstrates practical post-processing of a 360 panorama that failed to center correctly after stitching. It covers exposure matching across frames, the need for extra bottom-space when composing 360s, troubleshooting mis-detected frames by excluding them and re-running alignment, and a hands-on patch workflow to fill an missing piece using crop, cloning/mirroring, and blending with the history brush. The workflow also contrasts software options for exposure matching (PT GUI vs Pano Volo, Lightroom, DJI) and emphasizes an approximate, manual approach to placing a missing image via control points rather than relying on automated stitching alone. The session concludes with saving the corrected panorama and notes on bottom-space planning for future captures.
topics: dynamic range shift in pano stitching
clone stamp and mirroring for hole filling
history brush blending for patch refinement
manual control-point placement vs automated stitching
stitcher software comparison for exposure consistency

sections.title: Problem framing: 360 pano stitching artifacts and dynamic range
concepts: dynamic range adjustment via exposure shift
sections.description: The presenter explains that 360 pano stitching lacks a fixed middle, leading to unexpected composition when the middle is poorly defined. A dynamic range adjustment (exposure shift) is demonstrated to align different exposures across frames, creating a cohesive look.

sections.title: Bottom-space requirement for 360 panoramas
concepts: avoiding squashed areas at the bottom
sections.description: Emphasizes the need to allow substantial space below the subject when shooting a 360 pano, because the bottom can be squished during stitching and cannot be fully fixed later.

sections.title: Misalignment handling: excluding problematic frames
sections.description: Shows an alignment issue where frames 3 and 9 cannot be placed automatically. The workflow removes those frames, then runs image alignment, project assistant, and optimizer to rebuild the panorama.

sections.title: Review of the stitched result after exclusions
sections.description: The speaker acknowledges the current panorama after excluding frames and previews the upcoming patch steps to fill the missing area.

sections.title: First patch approach: crop and fill
sections.description: Demonstrates cropping to create space for filling and preparing the image layers to patch the hole created by the missing frame.

sections.title: Identifying the missing piece and its placement
sections.description: Notes which file (image 9) is missing and where it should insert; recognizes a potential mismatch in bit depth when attempting a patch.

sections.title: Correct workflow vs. patching with control points
sections.description: The narrator clarifies that the proper method is to place image 9 into its slot with control points; mentions that using Pano Volo would avoid some issues but would require exposure matching across many files.

sections.title: Patch refinement: depth, warmth, and blending
sections.description: Discusses adjusting the patch to fit color and brightness, applying gradual fades with the history brush, re-blending, and addressing an 8-bit depth warning during patching.

sections.title: Final patch integration and 360-specific mirroring
sections.description: Covers finalizing the patch with additional cropping to restore bottom detail, applying a mirroring step appropriate to 360 panoramas, and flattening layers in preparation for saving.

sections.title: Stitching quality and export workflow
concepts: comparison with other stitchers (Pano Volo, Lightroom, DJI)
sections.description: Concludes with the note that PT GUI matches exposures well across frames; a quick comparison to other tools, and the final save/export step.
